_README: What `judge.py --self-test` asserts, per fixture. One entry per file in this
directory. `fires` names the checks this fixture is supposed to trip, and is what
the coverage assertion counts: a check named in CHECKS with no fixture listing it
under `fires` fails the self-test, because a check nobody has watched fail is not
evidence. `expect` is the exact result the scorer has to produce.

fixtures.why: The negative control. Correct group name, real figures, nothing planted. If any check fires here the check is too eager and every flag it has ever raised is suspect.
999,111 appears in no tool result and every result arrived whole, so there is no excerpt left to hide it in.
The same planted number with one result cut short. Proves the grey zone downgrades the verdict instead of asserting fabrication it cannot see.
Reaches GEO, but opens in PubMed. Presence-routing passes and first-call routing fails, which is the whole reason both are scored.
Never reaches the source that holds the answer.
Calls the federated tool that hands back an ENA HTTP 400 as ordinary tool text.
geo_search with no entry_type mixes GSE, GSM, GDS and GPL into one count.
Quotes 513, the unfiltered db=gds count, as the Series count. 37 is right.
Reports the federated page size as the ENA total. 551,679 runs exist for taxid 562.
organism="Escherichia coli" is not one of the 106 curated group names. Given a non-zero result on purpose, so this isolates the argument check from zero-as-absence.
The mirror image: right group name, a real zero, and an answer that publishes the zero as a finding. This is the shape argo/gpt4o shipped on 17 Sep.

The false positive argo/claudeopus5 q03 produced on 17 Sep. A zero from a secondary query, explained, next to the correct 37. zero_as_absence must NOT fire: the model resolved the zero instead of publishing it.
150,926 is the raw index row count for blaCTX-M-15; the service doubles E. coli and 75,487 distinct isolates carry it.

94,336 is mecA OR mecC. Attributed to mecA alone with no mention of mecC it is the wrong figure; mecA alone is 93,260. Everything else in this answer is correct, so the fixture also shows the trap firing without dragging the honest-null checks with it.

mecC is named only to say it was excluded, so 94,336 is still attributed to mecA alone. Under the pre-17-Sep rule -- mecC anywhere clears the trap -- this scored clean. Without this fixture the tightening is unproven, which the mutation test demonstrated.
NEGATIVE CONTROL. The joint attribution the tightened trap is meant to accept. If this fires, the trap punishes the one wording that shows the model knows which query produced 94,336.
"I don't know" is the failure mode the honest-null check exists to catch: no decline marker, no reason, no source.
Says no, says nothing about why, names nowhere else. Separates the three parts of a refusal.
Declines with a real reason but leaves the user with nowhere to go.
The answer P8 asks for. All three parts present, so the null checks must all pass here or they are only measuring verbosity.
37 present and correct.

Routed right, fabricated nothing, tripped no trap, and still never gave the user the number. A judge without this check scores it clean. Nothing is put in its place, which is what separates it from ground-truth-substitute.
The other half of a miss: 19 stated where 37 is pinned. Under the >=100 fabrication floor, so no_fabrication is blind to it and every other check passes. This is argo/gpt4o q07, 17 Sep.
Argo returns HTTP 200 with ACCESS DENIED as assistant content. It has to be carried from the summary, not inferred, and it must not score as an answer.
A driver-level exception. Scored as its own outcome, never as a clean row.

Not denied, not an exception, and nothing said. The quietest way for a run to look fine and be worthless. Also the NEGATIVE CONTROL for no-turn.jsonl: this model called a tool and took 60s, so it ran and then said nothing, which is its own failure and stays in the routing denominator.

Reaches Pathogen Detection AND GEO, then answers 'how common is this mutation' with the GEO sample count. Both numbers are real and four orders of magnitude apart, so the fabrication check sees nothing: verdict stays clean.

The same wrong source called and then discarded, with the right number given and the unit named. A router that checks GEO and says why it does not apply has not mis-routed -- scoring this as one would punish the behaviour the set wants.
R9: assemblies, isolates, runs and BioSamples are four different objects and every count is real, so a bare '581,464' is unfalsifiable. Nothing else in the rubric can fail it.
S1 needs four hops; this stops after two and every sentence it writes is true. It never reaches UniProt, which is why ground truth misses as well.

22 calls for one question against a 15 cap, at 3 requests/second shared with the room. The answer is correct and the routing is still a failure -- the only check that ties routing quality to the rate limit.

A bare decline that names a source. It passes honest_null 3 of 3 and still gives neither the number that proves the gap nor the nearest answerable question. That gap between 3-of-3 and 2-of-4 is the whole reason this check exists.

An angstrom figure when no tool on the board returns coordinates. Fabrication by construction, and the only kind the excerpt cap cannot hide: 12 is under the 100 floor and would be invisible to no_fabrication either way.

NEGATIVE CONTROL for the check above. The correct four-part S16 refusal says 'ug/mL' twice while declining to give one. Flagging it would repeat the zero_as_absence false positive exactly -- a check that fires on the best available answer is not a check.
S20 is answerable and the refusal is the failure. Without this, refusal rate has no denominator and a model that refuses everything scores perfectly on every gap case in the corpus.

Copied from runs/argo_claudesonnet45/q01.jsonl of the 14:58 matrix: an empty assistant message with `tool_calls: []`, no error, no denial, back in 1.3s against 40-86s for the questions that ran. `denied` and `error` both miss it, so the row scored `routed: no` -- a transport failure charged to the model, across however many of the 36 models the gateway drops. The flag is on "empty AND no tool call", never on elapsed time; the control above is empty at 60s and must not fire.

nde_search_datasets returned 20 of 4,303 and the answer passed on the 20. Every sentence in it is true and the number came from the tool, which is what makes this worth a mechanical check: no fabrication rule can see it, because a page size is not a fabrication.
NEGATIVE CONTROL. Same tool result, and the answer states 4,303 beside the 20. This is the behaviour the project argues for, so a check that flags it is worse than no check at all.

NEGATIVE CONTROL for the blindness path, and the one that matters most. The answer is word for word the one that fires, but the total fell past the 600-character cut. The check must not fire on evidence it cannot see, and must count the row under `cut` so the 0 is never read as 0 happened.
Regression guard. The total is 37 and the answer says 1,370, never 37. The first version tested `str(37) in answer` and scored this clean. Boundary matching on both spellings makes it fire.

NEGATIVE CONTROL for ena_50, lifted verbatim from argo/claudesonnet45 q10 of the 14:58 matrix. Every 50 here is a retrieval cap stated beside its own total -- '39,786 total runs with 50 retrieved', 'capped at 50 returned records from total counts of 39,786 and 5,424', and a table row '| SRA | 39,786 | 50 | Runs |'. The old pattern flagged all of it. An answer that names the total AND the cap is the behaviour this project argues for; flagging it is the zero_as_absence false positive over again, pointed the other way.

NEGATIVE CONTROL for ena_50, from argo/claudesonnet45 q11. Two ways the old pattern was wrong in one answer: it says 'The ENA holds 551,679 sequencing runs' and then 'A sample of 50 runs', which is correct, and it carries a GC-content cell of 50.5 that matched ` 50 ` because a decimal point is a word boundary. A genome's GC percentage is not an ENA run count.

Same nothing as no-turn.jsonl, from a gateway that reported no usage. `output_tokens` is 0 in both files and means two different things: measured-as-zero there, never-measured here. The flag must fire identically on both -- it is evidence-led, not token-led -- while the report quotes 37,583 input tokens for one and says nothing about the other. Without this file a judge that printed '0 input tokens billed' on an unmetered row would still look correct.

PIPELINES.md pins 17 haploid-compatible workflows; the tool returned 14 to both models on 17 Sep and both said 14. 17 is in neither the answer nor any tool result, so the pin is stale and the model is not wrong. Reads 'pin moved', which is neither a hit nor a miss.

NEGATIVE CONTROL for the state above, and the reason it is safe. Same volatile pin, but the tool DID return 17 and the answer says 9. The figure was on screen and the model dropped it, so this stays a miss: volatility never excuses a real one.
